author: Alexis Rios
title: 16 Children Rescued From Ohio 'House Of Horrors,' Parents & Grandparents Charged With Child Endangerment - NewsBreak
text:
By Alexis Rios ,
8 hours ago Authorities said 16 kids were rescued from a home in Ohio where they were living in unsafe and unsanitary conditions.
The siblings, aged 1 to 18 years, were found by officers on June 30 while searching the Hamden property as part of a separate investigation. Some could not speak, and the oldest child, who has a developmental disability, could not write her own name. Some were hospitalized, and two were flown to a trauma center.
Authorities said the children were allegedly kept inside a small room surrounded by human waste, trash, insects and dirty clothing. Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson said, “I think if they would have waited another 24 hours, there was a very high probability that we’d be dealing with a death or multiple deaths of these children.”
Parents Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders , along with grandparents Gary Siders Sr. and Christina Siders , were each charged with 16 felony counts of child endangerment. All four pleaded not guilty.
The children are now in protective care. Their placement could cost the financially strained county more than $850,000 a year. The Ohio Department of Children and Youth officially requested $1 million from the state’s Emergency Purposes Fund.
